card.name: Right before excess-effect outcomes
card.fires_on: Partway through drug names or small words in interaction and overdose sentences, where the next words are likely to describe too much exposure, too high levels or added risk. The marked word is often a piece of a drug name or the word 'the' after 'increase'.

modes.label: Inside drug names
modes.description: Middle piece of a drug name in an interaction sentence that says exposure is increased.
modes.example: Gemfibrozil significantly increased repag<<lin>>ide exposures by 8.1 fold

modes.label: After increase or may lead to
modes.description: Small linking word or letter in a sentence saying a combination raises a risk or effect.
modes.example: insulin may increase<< the>> risk of hypoglycemia.

modes.label: Levels above or below target
modes.description: Word about levels in overdose or monitoring text where levels go beyond the desired range.
modes.example: Epogen overdosage can cause<< hem>>oglobin levels above the desired level, which

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words meaning too much or excess, and away from words meaning lacking or failing.
card.plain: It fires in drug-interaction and overdose sentences just before the text says something is raised too much.
